title: Quarterly deployment prioritization and OKR translation for enterprise Private/VPC/on-prem
creator: Maya Thompson
description: This ticket captures the quarter-level prioritization and OKR translation for enterprise deployment capabilities (Private control plane, VPC improvements, and on-prem packaging). Goal: deliver a focused slice of features that materially reduce sales friction for enterprise deals and improve self-serve conversions for regulated customers. We will map each candidate feature to measurable OKRs, estimate engineering effort, call out trade-offs, and produce a sequenced delivery plan for 2026-Q2.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prioritized feature list mapped to 3 OKRs with measurable targets; 2) Detailed milestones (monthly) and owners assigned; 3) Eng dependencies validated and rough estimates committed; 4) Security and compliance gating items identified and triaged; 5) Draft PRD and design artifacts linked and reviewed by stakeholders.
milestones: Milestone 1 (Apr): Finalize PRD and OKR mappings, secure engineering commitment and sprint allocation
Milestone 2 (May): Complete core VPC connectivity improvements (peering and routing), KMS integration MVP, and RBAC design spec
Milestone 3 (Jun): Private control plane beta rollout to 3 pilot customers, run upgrade/rollback drills, gather OKR telemetry
okr_mapping: OKR-Platform-1: Increase enterprise private adoption — Target: onboard 6 new paid Private customers by EoQ (contributes to revenue +1.2M ARR)
OKR-Platform-2: Improve reliability for private customers — Target: reduce Private P99 end-to-end request latency by 10% and increase uptime to 99.95%
OKR-Platform-3: Reduce sales friction — Target: decrease average enterprise onboarding time from 14 days to 7 days via improved docs, installer, and KMS integrations
tradeoffs: Tradeoff A: Prioritize VPC-first features (peering, KMS, RBAC) over a fully automated air-gap installer. Rationale: VPC improvements unlock faster revenue and serviceability for most enterprise customers; air-gap remains high-effort with narrower TAM.
Tradeoff B: Defer advanced on-prem day-2 automation (cluster autoscaling, self-upgrade) to next quarter to ensure security gating and KMS stability for GA.
Tradeoff C: Opt for phased GA (beta -> GA) to collect telemetry and avoid broad blast radius; this increases manual lift for pilots but lowers risk
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KMS integration delays could block GA. Mitigation: start security review in parallel and ship KMS as opt-in during beta with fallback to customer-managed secrets.
Risk: Capacity and infra for private pilots could strain support. Mitigation: reserve Dedicated pool quota and document runbooks for pilot handoffs.

Risk: Regulatory needs for air-gapped customers are underestimated. Mitigation: create a focused discovery sprint with one anchor customer to validate requirements before committing to automation work.
